paragraphs.text: Then after the space of fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me.
paragraphs.original: Ἔπειτα διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν πάλιν ἀνέβην εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα μετὰ Βαρναβᾶ συμπαραλαβὼν καὶ Τίτον·
paragraphs.translit: Epeita dia dekatessarōn etōn palin anebēn eis Hierosolyma meta Barnaba symparalabōn kai Titon·

paragraphs.text: And I went up by revelation; and I laid before them the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles but privately before them who were of repute, lest by any means I should be running, or had run, in vain.
paragraphs.original: ἀνέβην δὲ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν· καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ κηρύσσω ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, κατʼ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν, μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ ἔδραμον.
paragraphs.translit: anebēn de kata apokalypsin· kai anethemēn autois to euangelion ho kēryssō en tois ethnesin, katʼ idian de tois dokousin, mē pōs eis kenon trechō ē edramon.

paragraphs.text: But not even Titus who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ Τίτος ὁ σὺν ἐμοί, Ἕλλην ὤν, ἠναγκάσθη περιτμηθῆναι·
paragraphs.translit: allʼ oude Titos ho syn emoi, Hellēn ōn, ēnankasthē peritmēthēnai·

paragraphs.text: and that because of the false brethren privily brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
paragraphs.original: διὰ δὲ τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους, οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον κατασκοπῆσαι τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἡμῶν ἣν ἔχομεν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα ἡμᾶς καταδουλώσουσιν—
paragraphs.translit: dia de tous pareisaktous pseudadelphous, hoitines pareisēlthon kataskopēsai tēn eleutherian hēmōn hēn echomen en Christō Iēsou, hina hēmas katadoulōsousin—

paragraphs.text: to whom we gave place in the way of subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
paragraphs.original: οἷς οὐδὲ πρὸς ὥραν εἴξαμεν τῇ ὑποταγῇ, ἵνα ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου διαμείνῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: hois oude pros hōran eixamen tē hypotagē, hina hē alētheia tou euangeliou diameinē pros hymas.

paragraphs.text: But from those who were reputed to be somewhat (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth not man`s person)-- they, I say, who were of repute imparted nothing to me:
paragraphs.original: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν δοκούντων εἶναί τι— ὁποῖοί ποτε ἦσαν οὐδέν μοι διαφέρει· πρόσωπον θεὸς ἀνθρώπου οὐ λαμβάνει— ἐμοὶ γὰρ οἱ δοκοῦντες οὐδὲν προσανέθεντο,
paragraphs.translit: apo de tōn dokountōn einai ti— hopoioi pote ēsan ouden moi diapherei· prosōpon theos anthrōpou ou lambanei— emoi gar hoi dokountes ouden prosanethento,

paragraphs.text: but contrariwise, when they saw that I had been intrusted with the gospel of the uncircumcision, even as Peter with [the gospel] of the circumcision
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον ἰδόντες ὅτι πεπίστευμαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἀκροβυστίας καθὼς Πέτρος τῆς περιτομῆς,
paragraphs.translit: alla tounantion idontes hoti pepisteumai to euangelion tēs akrobystias kathōs Petros tēs peritomēs,

paragraphs.text: (for he that wrought for Peter unto the apostleship of the circumcision wrought for me also unto the Gentiles);
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐνεργήσας Πέτρῳ εἰς ἀποστολὴν τῆς περιτομῆς ἐνήργησεν καὶ ἐμοὶ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη,
paragraphs.translit: ho gar energēsas Petrō eis apostolēn tēs peritomēs enērgēsen kai emoi eis ta ethnē,

paragraphs.text: and when they perceived the grace that was given unto me, James and Cephas and John, they who were reputed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that we should go unto the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision;
paragraphs.original: καὶ γνόντες τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Ἰωάννης, οἱ δοκοῦντες στῦλοι εἶναι, δεξιὰς ἔδωκαν ἐμοὶ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ κοινωνίας, ἵνα ἡμεῖς εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, αὐτοὶ δὲ εἰς τὴν περιτομήν·
paragraphs.translit: kai gnontes tēn charin tēn dotheisan moi, Iakōbos kai Kēphas kai Iōannēs, hoi dokountes styloi einai, dexias edōkan emoi kai Barnaba koinōnias, hina hēmeis eis ta ethnē, autoi de eis tēn peritomēn·

paragraphs.text: only [they would] that we should remember the poor; which very thing I was also zealous to do.
paragraphs.original: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν, ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: monon tōn ptōchōn hina mnēmoneuōmen, ho kai espoudasa auto touto poiēsai.

paragraphs.text: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I resisted him to the face, because he stood condemned.
paragraphs.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην, ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν·
paragraphs.translit: Hote de ēlthen Kēphas eis Antiocheian, kata prosōpon autō antestēn, hoti kategnōsmenos ēn·

paragraphs.text: For before that certain came from James, he ate with the Gentiles; but when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing them that were of the circumcision.
paragraphs.original: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν· ὅτε δὲ ἦλθον, ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν, φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς.
paragraphs.translit: pro tou gar elthein tinas apo Iakōbou meta tōn ethnōn synēsthien· hote de ēlthon, hypestellen kai aphōrizen heauton, phoboumenos tous ek peritomēs.

paragraphs.text: And the rest of the Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation.
paragraphs.original: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρναβᾶς συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.
paragraphs.translit: kai synypekrithēsan autō kai hoi loipoi Ioudaioi, hōste kai Barnabas synapēchthē autōn tē hypokrisei.

paragraphs.text: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Cephas before [them] all, If thou, being a Jew, livest as do the Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, how compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων· Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς καὶ οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς, πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις Ἰουδαΐζειν;
paragraphs.translit: allʼ hote eidon hoti ouk orthopodousin pros tēn alētheian tou euangeliou, eipon tō Kēpha emprosthen pantōn· Ei sy Ioudaios hyparchōn ethnikōs kai ouk Ioudaikōs zēs, pōs ta ethnē anankazeis Ioudaizein;

paragraphs.text: We being Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,
paragraphs.original: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί,
paragraphs.translit: Hēmeis physei Ioudaioi kai ouk ex ethnōn hamartōloi,

paragraphs.text: yet knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, even we believed on Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ, and not by the works of the law: because by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
paragraphs.original: εἰδότες δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σάρξ.
paragraphs.translit: eidotes de hoti ou dikaioutai anthrōpos ex ergōn nomou ean mē dia pisteōs Iēsou Christou, kai hēmeis eis Christon Iēsoun episteusamen, hina dikaiōthōmen ek pisteōs Christou kai ouk ex ergōn nomou, hoti ex ergōn nomou ou dikaiōthēsetai pasa sarx.

paragraphs.text: But if, while we sought to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Christ a minister of sin? God forbid.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος; μὴ γένοιτο·
paragraphs.translit: ei de zētountes dikaiōthēnai en Christō heurethēmen kai autoi hamartōloi, ara Christos hamartias diakonos; mē genoito·

paragraphs.text: For if I build up again those things which I destroyed, I prove myself a transgressor.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ, παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν συνιστάνω.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar ha katelysa tauta palin oikodomō, parabatēn emauton synistanō.

paragraphs.text: For I through the law died unto the law, that I might live unto God.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον ἵνα θεῷ ζήσω· Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι·
paragraphs.translit: egō gar dia nomou nomō apethanon hina theō zēsō· Christō synestaurōmai·

paragraphs.text: I have been crucified with Christ; and it is no longer I that live, but Christ living in me: and that [life] which I now live in the flesh I live in faith, [the faith] which is in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.
paragraphs.original: ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός· ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: zō de ouketi egō, zē de en emoi Christos· ho de nyn zō en sarki, en pistei zō tē tou hyiou tou theou tou agapēsantos me kai paradontos heauton hyper emou.

paragraphs.text: I do not make void the grace of God: for if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nought.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰ γὰρ διὰ νόμου δικαιοσύνη, ἄρα Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν.
paragraphs.translit: ouk athetō tēn charin tou theou· ei gar dia nomou dikaiosynē, ara Christos dōrean apethanen.
